The working file is the complete analysis; the reports are reader copies of it. Each should be read in full — this message is not the analysis.

In brief: the claim is **false as literally worded, and true only under specific, undisclosed reinterpretations**. The physically achievable electricity-to-electricity round-trip efficiency for this system is ~17–41% (the Carnot ceiling for the discharge leg alone is ~62–64%, not the ~33% a naive reading of "290°C" would imply, and still far below 85%). The best disclosed real-world commercial power-to-power figure (Malta Inc., read at source) tops out at "up to 60%" — the >85% figures that do appear in the literature apply only to cogeneration (heat+power) operation, not pure electricity round-trip. On cost, a genuinely 5 MWh-scale molten-salt system sits roughly two orders of magnitude below this technology's commercially-proven scale and is estimated at 2–15× more expensive per kWh of delivered electricity than a same-capacity lithium-ion BESS, even in the most favorable case tested. Overall confidence is LOW, driven mainly by several cost-side ground truths this session could not confirm at a primary source (two WebFetch attempts failed with 403/DNS errors); the technical (efficiency) half of the verdict rests on a HIGH-confidence physical-law chain and is essentially unaffected by that uncertainty.
